statement: Use z=s-1/2 and Xi(z)=xi(1/2+z); Xi is even. A nontrivial zero is z=eta+i*gamma, with RH equivalent to eta=0 for every zero.
title: Centered zeta coordinate

statement: Define D(E)=Xi(sqrt(-E)). A zero rho=1/2+eta+i*gamma maps to E=gamma^2-eta^2-2i*eta*gamma. RH is equivalent to all zero energies being positive real.
title: Squared-energy map

statement: If the squared energies are positive real, m(E)=-D'(E)/D(E) is Stieltjes/Herglotz and inverse-energy moments generate PSD Hankel matrices.
title: Inverse-energy Stieltjes moments

statement: For an isolated conjugate pair E=r exp(+-i theta), the first 2x2 inverse-energy Hankel determinant is strictly negative when theta is nonzero.
title: Complex energy pair forces Hankel negativity

statement: For omega>0 define Theta_omega(z)=xi(1/2-omega-iz)/xi(1/2+omega-iz). On the real boundary its modulus is one unconditionally.
title: Zeta scattering ratio

statement: An off-line zero rho=beta+i gamma creates a pole z=-gamma+i(beta-1/2-omega) of Theta_omega. It enters the upper half-plane when beta-1/2>omega.
title: Off-line zero becomes scattering pole

statement: The Cayley transform M_omega=i(1+Theta_omega)/(1-Theta_omega) converts Schur contractivity into Herglotz/Pick positivity. A full all-omega passivity criterion is RH-equivalent in the intended canonical-system setting.
title: Cayley passivity formulation

statement: Boundary unitarity alone cannot imply RH because off-line zeros can be hidden in Blaschke/all-pass factors with unit boundary modulus.
title: Boundary unitarity no-go

statement: For a=eta+i gamma in the right half-plane, B_a(z)=(z-a)/(z+conj(a)) is all-pass on the imaginary axis and its phase derivative is a positive Lorentzian.
title: Blaschke factor for an off-line zero

statement: At probe depth x>0, an off-line zero contributes the positive Green potential g_x(a)=-log|B_a(x)|.
title: Blaschke Green potential

statement: The Balazard-Saias-Yor criterion expresses a critical-line logarithmic integral as a positive sum over zeros with beta>1/2, and RH is equivalent to its vanishing.
title: BSY positive defect

statement: A simple conjugate off-line zero pair contributes a real rank-two residue block with signature (1,1); m distinct simple pairs give exact finite residue signature (m,m) under linear independence of the exponential modes.
title: Pair residue inertia

statement: Off-line displacement eta produces paired growth/decay factors whose symmetric defect is cosh(eta T); residue norms grow exponentially like exp(2 eta T).
title: Hyperbolic defect growth

statement: A symmetric off-line pair at 1/2+-eta+i gamma contributes a horizontal log|xi| gradient term negative exactly inside a disk of radius |eta| centered on the critical line at height gamma.
title: Horizontal gradient defect disk

statement: For E(x)=psi(x)-x, M(w)=int_1^infinity E(x)^2 x^{-w-1} dx has convergence abscissa 2 Theta, where Theta=sup Re rho. Thus RH iff the critical finite-volume Green energy grows only logarithmically.
title: Prime Green energy

statement: With b_n=Lambda(n)-1 and A_N=psi(N)-N, summation by parts gives a positive quadratic Green energy with kernel max(m,n)^(-s).
title: Discrete Green quadratic form

statement: The diagonal weighted prime noise is asymptotically 1/2 log^2 X, so RH-scale total Green energy requires the off-diagonal covariance to cancel that leading term.
title: Diagonal shot-noise cancellation requirement

statement: The weighted average of the Hardy-Littlewood singular series has a universal -1/2 log H secondary bias, which supplies exactly the leading anti-correlation needed to screen diagonal shot noise in the model.
title: Hardy-Littlewood secondary screening

statement: Define the weighted actual-minus-Hardy-Littlewood pair-correlation remainder R_q(X). A rigorous subpower bound R_q(X)=X^{o(1)} for one fixed q, together with the controlled model contribution, would imply RH.
title: Screening remainder target

statement: In T=log x coordinates, h(T)=e^{-T/2}(psi(e^T)-e^T) satisfies a first-order stable filter equation driven by the centered prime impulse train.
title: Prime error as stable-filter output

statement: Under RH the normalized prime-error state h(T) is B^2 almost periodic with frequencies gamma, and translations are unitary with generator P=-i d/dT. RH failure corresponds to an exponentially growing mode that is not in the mean-square Hilbert space.
title: Besicovitch translation formulation

statement: For q>0, L_q(X)=sum_{n>=2}(Lambda(n)-1) exp(-(n/X)^q) has Mellin multiplier Gamma(s/q)/q; a zero rho contributes -(m_rho/q)Gamma(rho/q)X^rho. The exact endpoint L_q(X)=O(X^1/2) is RH-equivalent for fixed q.
title: Safe Gamma filter

statement: Differentiating the safe Gamma filter gives a localized shell S_q(X)=q sum (Lambda(n)-1)(n/X)^q exp(-(n/X)^q). Its log-space kernel is a probability density and its Fourier transform is Gamma(1-i omega/q).
title: Localized Gamma shell

statement: The localized shell has log-prime width about 1/q and effective zero-frequency bandwidth about q, giving Delta(log n) Delta(gamma) of order one.
title: Prime-zero uncertainty relation

statement: The global weighted L2 energy of the localized shell is a prime-pair quadratic form with an explicit positive sech kernel. q is exactly a multiplicative correlation-resolution parameter.
title: Exact multiplicative pair kernel

statement: Adding an exponential regulator delta gives an explicit positive multiplicative kernel K_{q,delta}; its convergence threshold is delta_c=2 Theta-1 and is independent of q.
title: Two-parameter susceptibility kernel

statement: Define c_j=-zeta'/zeta(2j+2)-zeta(2j+2)+1 and d_k=sum_{j=0}^k (-1)^j binom(k,j)c_j. Nörlund-Rice gives zero terms proportional to k! Gamma(1-rho/2)/Gamma(k+2-rho/2).
title: Safe binomial sequence

statement: All trivial-zero contributions to d_k sum to -1/(2k(k+1)); therefore corrected d_tilde_k=d_k+1/(2k(k+1)) isolates the nontrivial-zero spectrum to leading asymptotic order.
title: Trivial-zero correction

statement: Because zeta'/zeta has only simple poles even at multiple zeros and the Gamma coefficients decay exponentially in height, RH should be equivalent to bounded k^{3/4} d_tilde_k, without an epsilon or simplicity assumption.
title: Exact endpoint safe-binomial criterion

statement: The generating function of corrected d_k has a single boundary point z=1 whose indicial exponents are rho/2; after tau=-log(1-z), RH corresponds to purely oscillatory dilation modes.
title: Safe-binomial boundary singularity

statement: Normalize the Riemann theta kernel to a symmetric random variable X. Its moment generating function is xi(1/2+z)/xi(1/2); RH is exactly the Lee-Yang property that all zeros of this MGF are purely imaginary.
title: Theta Lee-Yang formulation

statement: The proposed infinite iterated curvature/log-concavity hierarchy fails for the actual Riemann theta kernel at higher iteration; it cannot serve as the RH route.
title: Iterated theta log-concavity fails

statement: Theta completion yields an explicit positive SUSY Schrödinger Hamiltonian H_+=-D^2+1/4+V_R=A^dagger A, but Xi is an interaction form factor rather than its spectral determinant.
title: SUSY theta Hamiltonian

statement: Constructing a positive or self-adjoint Hamiltonian from theta data is insufficient to prove RH; de Bruijn-Newman deformations can preserve positivity while permitting nonreal zeros.
title: Positive Hamiltonian no-go

statement: The conjugated radial modular-cusp operator is -D_x^2+1/4, and modular scattering contains zeta zeros as resonances. An off-line zero splits the paired resonance widths around the critical value.
title: Modular cusp resonance map

statement: For paired off-line modular resonances, normalized cusp coherence satisfies coherence^2=1-4 eta^2, so RH corresponds to perfect coherence in this two-mode model.
title: Cusp coherence defect

statement: For an off-line functional-equation pair with conjugate nonreal Hecke eigenvalues, any nondegenerate invariant Hermitian form has signature (1,1); a positive invariant metric would force the relevant eigenvalues real and hence eta=0.
title: Hecke invariant metric obstruction

statement: Toroidal Eisenstein periods select zeta zeros but do not constrain Re rho; toroidality alone cannot imply RH.
title: Toroidality alone no-go

statement: For G(z)=sum_{n>=1}(psi(n)-n)z^n and weighted coefficient norm sum |A_n|^2(n+1)^alpha, the critical smoothness exponent is alpha_*=-1-2 Theta; RH corresponds to alpha_*=-2.
title: Weighted-Dirichlet critical index

statement: At a safely convergent regulator, positive log-moments of the prime-error energy encode the distance to the rightmost singularity. Their factorial root growth recovers Theta.
title: Safe-point factorial moments

statement: Unit-width logarithmic block energies W_k have exponential growth rate 2 Theta-1. RH is equivalent to subexponential block energy.
title: Log-window energy criterion

statement: Numerical agreement, fitted exponents, synthetic-spectrum consistency, and LLM-generated derivations are evidence only. They cannot promote an RH-equivalent or new analytic claim to proved without a rigorous proof/certificate and independent review.
title: Research epistemic rule
